title: AI Movies Flop in Theaters, Even as AI Videos Flood Phones
summary:
There is an old saying in the film business: people would not pay to watch an actor in theaters if they could see them for free on TV. Today, AI-generated content in China is everywhere: a recent report suggests that among the explosion of microdramas in China, nearly two-thirds of those videos are all generated by AI.

But audiences seem to draw a line between what they will watch for free on their phones and what they will buy a ticket for. The fully AI-generated feature "Sanxingdui: Future Past" flopped at the Chinese box office, showing that AI still has a tough road ahead in theaters.

The film was no one-click project. Producer Bona says it was produced over two years by a team of 70 to 80 people, and some creators bristled at the idea that the images were created with a single click. The film was being tweaked and technically still "shooting" up until a week before it hit theaters. Still, that level of artistry was not evident on screen. An attendee told the international outlet AFP that the AI still "falls short" of a human-made, live-action production. "In the future, just like films, maybe decades later, it would get to a level when people are all willing to pay to watch," she said. "But for the moment, I think there would be very few who would."

A 100-minute feature also faces a hurdle short videos do not: it must go through a content review process before it can be screened in theaters, so the speed of bringing something new and fresh to market was not there for "Sanxingdui."

All eyes are now on the next test: YouTuber and AI creator Gossip Goblin's fully AI feature, "Gods Don't Give Gifts," opening in U.S. theaters this December and launching international sales at the American Film Market next month. It is the first such movie to receive a rating from the MPA, and it even intends to submit for eligibility at the Oscars for Best Animated Feature. Gossip Goblin has a large audience across psychedelic, sprawling AI shorts in a connected story universe, and hopes to draw a dedicated fanbase to theaters with a self-releasing strategy. Whether in China or America, people go to theaters expecting a level of cinematic quality above what they can get at home on their phones.
why_it_matters: The flop tests whether audiences will pay theater prices for AI-made films, and the answer could shape how much studios invest in AI features versus human-made movies.

keywords.explanation: Microdramas are very short drama videos, often watched on a phone.
The box office is the money a movie earns from ticket sales in theaters.
Live-action means a film made with real actors and cameras, not only animation.
A content review is an official check of a film before it is allowed to be shown.
A fanbase is the group of loyal fans who follow and support a creator's work.

background_read: Artificial intelligence tools can now create images, video and stories from instructions given by people.
Short videos made this way can be watched for free on phones, while a feature film shown in theaters is expected to look polished and feel like a complete story.
Making a film for theaters also takes extra steps, such as review before screening, which can slow down how quickly new work reaches audiences.
